account:
Today I have my normal mayoral appointments, including the mill grain inspection at ten and tea with my neighbour at three, plus an unusual civic presentation in the town hall great hall from eighteen hundred to eighteen thirty. The signed supplement says its subject is appreciation of municipal public service from the inn and local tradespeople. I am specifically asked to arrive at eighteen hundred, not earlier, so organisers can finish arrangements around their work. This looks like a planned appreciation gathering, possibly with a surprise element for me, rather than ordinary council business.

Yesterday I overheard the builder and baker confirm a private order for forty-four loaves, paid for with materials instead of emeralds. I saw the builder give the baker oak planks and a lantern. The baker declined to explain the occasion, leaving that to the customer. The innkeeper told me my presence at the presentation was all they needed and stressed the arrival time. The bread order may be refreshments for this gathering, and the materials may help the baker or be part of their barter, but I have not confirmed a connection.

The secretary has been arranging the formal appointment, requested a writable book, and used the book I supplied this morning to record the approved supplement. The secretary is now relaying approval to the innkeeper. The innkeeper, builder, baker and secretary are therefore involved in either the presentation or the unusual preparations I have observed, though I do not know everyone's exact role. My neighbour has mentioned asking around about riverside improvements but has no firm suggestions; I have no evidence that this is connected. I should keep my ordinary appointments and attend the presentation at the requested time.
